elements.id-string-9: \markboth{IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence} {Huang \MakeLowercase{\textit{et al.}}: Domain-Scalable Unpaired Image Translation via Latent Space Anchoring}
elements.id-string-11: Unpaired image-to-image translation (UNIT) aims to map images between two visual domains without paired training data.
elements.id-string-12: However, given a UNIT model trained on certain domains, it is difficult for current methods to incorporate new domains because they often need to train the full model on both existing and new domains.
elements.id-string-13: To address this problem, we propose a new domain-scalable UNIT method, termed as \emph{latent space anchoring}, which can be efficiently extended to new visual domains and does not need to fine-tune encoders and decoders of existing domains.
elements.id-string-14: Our method anchors images of different domains to the same latent space of frozen GANs by learning lightweight encoder and regressor models to reconstruct single-domain images.
elements.id-string-15: In the inference phase, the learned encoders and decoders of different domains can be arbitrarily combined to translate images between any two domains without fine-tuning.
elements.id-string-16: Experiments on various datasets show that the proposed method achieves superior performance on both standard and domain-scalable UNIT tasks in comparison with the state-of-the-art methods.
elements.id-string-18: Unsupervised image-to-image translation, multi-domain image translation, semantic structure alignment, GANs prior.
elements.id-string-20: \begin{figure}[t]  \includegraphics[width=1\linewidth]{figs/task_v4.pdf} \caption{An illustration of the image-to-image translation paradigms. \textbf{(a)} Dual-domain paired image translation, \eg, Pix2Pix~\cite{pix2pix} and SPADE \cite{spade}, learns a one-way mapping $T_{A \rightarrow B}$ from domain $A$ to domain $B$. \textbf{(b)} Dual-domain unpaired image translation, \eg, CycleGAN~\cite{cyclegan} and UNIT \cite{unit}, learns a bi-directional mapping $T_{A \rightarrow B}$ and $T_{B \rightarrow A}$ between two domains. \textbf{(c)} Many-to-many unpaired image translation, \eg, StarGAN~\cite{cyclegan} and DRIT++ \cite{drit++}, learns mappings between any two domains via a shared feature space $H$, encoders $E_{\{A,B,C\}}$, and decoders $D_{\{A,B,C\}}$. \textbf{(d)} Our latent space anchoring method learns mappings between any two domains via the latent space $p(z)$ of a frozen GAN $G$. }  \end{figure}
elements.id-string-21: \begin{figure}[t]  \hspace{-1.4em} \includegraphics[width=1.04\linewidth]{figs/task2_v1.pdf} \caption{Adding a new domain $X$ to a learned UNIT model. \darkred{Red}: Models that need to be fine-tuned. \blue{Blue}: Models that need to be trained from scratch. \textbf{(a)} Existing methods usually need to fine-tune the full model on data of all available image domains. \textbf{(b)} Our method only needs to learn an encoder $E_{X}^{new}$ and a decoder $D_{X}^{new}$ on data of the new domain $X$, then images of the domain $X$ can be translated from/to previous domains via the latent space of the generator. }  \end{figure}

elements.id-string-30: We propose a domain-scalable challenge of UNIT methods --- to give the models an improved flexibility to extend into new domains without training the full model on the data of all available domains.We present a novel UNIT method named latent space anchoring to tackle the  challenging task.
elements.id-string-31: It aligns the semantic structures of multi-domain images by  reconstructing single-domain images from the latent space of frozen GANs.We conduct comprehensive experiments on various image domains, UNIT tasks, and different powerful GANs backbones.
elements.id-string-32: Qualitative and quantitative comparisons with the state-of-the-art methods, as well as the user study, validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

elements.id-string-37: We use a lightweight Encoder$_C$ to map the visual domain to GAN's latent space (Sec.~\ref{sec:encode}), then use a lightweight Regressor$_C$ to reconstruct input images from GAN's latent space.
elements.id-string-38: We show that it is equivalent to aligning the perceptual structures of images of different domains.\textbf{(c)} During inference, we can use the trained encoder and regressor to perform translation between any two domains, as well as generate well-aligned multi-domain images by sampling from the GAN's latent space.}
